issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a 'Milkable' interface (with method messageOnMilk()), but the solution repository introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (declaring messageOnMilk()) and leaves Milkable.java empty. This naming mismatch (and the empty Milkable file) is a structural inconsistency: students following the specification will implement or use 'Milkable', while the solution uses 'Dairy', causing confusion and compilation/type mismatches between expected and actual types.
issues.suggestedFix: Make interface naming consistent with the problem specification: either rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' and have Goat and Seal implement Milkable, or update the problem statement/UML to refer to 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. Also ensure Milkable.java (or Dairy.java) contains the correct method signature 'String messageOnMilk()' and remove any empty/unused placeholder file.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable', but the solution repository defines and uses an interface named 'Dairy' (e.g., classes implement Dairy). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual interface (objects that can be milked) creates a mapping confusion for students when comparing the task description and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (file Dairy.java -> Milkable.java, and update all implementing classes to 'implements Milkable'), or alternatively provide a Milkable interface in the solution that matches the problem statement and have Dairy delegate to it. Ensure the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use 'Milkable'.
